title: Redundant Sensor Masks Link Failure
summary: A duplicated sensor hides an underdetermined split. A forced-zero check exposes the contradiction, and an independent difference sensor restores a unique solution.
concept: A repeated measurement adds no information. When a link is forced to zero, a duplicated sensor can no longer agree with the unchanged total — the reduced row exposes 0 = 1.
equations: failed: x₂ = 0, but the duplicate sensor reports 210

normal.label: Normal state
normal.description: Two sensors report the same 100 Mbps total, but one is only double the other, so the split stays underdetermined.

failed.label: Link failed
failed.description: The backup link is forced to x₂ = 0 while the duplicate sensor still reports 210 Mbps. No split can satisfy both readings.

corrected.label: Corrected (simulated)
corrected.description: An independent difference measurement replaces the duplicate sensor, producing the unique split x₁ = 60, x₂ = 40.

teachingNotes: A doubled equation is redundant: it looks like a second measurement but carries no new information.
The failed stage reduces to a contradiction row, which is mathematical proof that the readings cannot all be true.
Recovery here is a modelled change of measurement, not a physical repair of any device.
